items.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005
items.q: Frankie Trumbauer and I sat next, together, and that was it, he was a wonderful guy and a wonderful player.

ctx.x: How much did it cost for a room for a week in New York at that time.

Oh well with the Whiteman band hotel rooms were so reasonable. We used to get a rate. $2.50 single. Not the Waldorf, but good hotels. No flea bags. Like Goldie used to say, no flea bags you know. And it was great traveling with the band, the Whiteman band. And I’ll never forget. See I joined spring of ’36. But I was doing the radio show. Woodbury Hollow Soap Hour. And I just did that. The rest of the band, they were doing Jumbo. Billy Rose’s Jumbo at the Hippodrome Theater, it was on Sixth Avenue just north of…
What was he like? Was he friendly? Easy to get along with?

items.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995
items.q: Frankie Trumbauer and I sat next to each other.

ctx.x: Well, Ernie, a sax player, came to me at WINS when WINS, oh, all the networks had live music. Six piece band, eight piece band, forty, whatever. He comes to me and he says, “You know, Al, Benny Bonacchio is going to leave the Whiteman band.” Benny took Chet Haslett’s place, and he’s going to need a first alto player.” I says, “You’ve got to be kidding.” He says, “No, go see him.” So he made an appointment and I went to see him up in Studio 3A, third floor of NBC. This is early 1936. So Paul Whiteman greeted me…
Isn’t that interesting. You see the difference in the ages right there.
